data.hypothesis: The baseline assigns one output to each thread in a 32x32 CTA, with neighboring lanes advancing across rows and therefore accessing row-major A and C with strides. This candidate keeps the same 32x32 output footprint but maps lanes across columns and assigns four rows at one column to each thread. That reuses each loaded B value across four independent FP32 accumulators and may improve coalescing while reducing CTA threads from 1024 to 256; the additional per-thread state may affect occupancy. The baseline is the measured one-output-per-thread control; candidate performance remains unmeasured.
data.notes: The implementation handles row/column tails, applies alpha and beta once per output, and leaves the entry point, buffers, and default-stream launch behavior intact. No candidate correctness or timing result is available yet; baseline-e1 was correct with a 0.2734838867186667 s mean.
transformations: Map each CTA to the same 32x32 output tile as the baseline using a 32x8 block; each thread computes four rows at one column.
Maintain four independent FP32 accumulators per thread and reuse the per-K B value across those outputs; lane columns access B and C contiguously.
Guard row/column tails, use size_t for matrix offsets, and apply alpha/beta once for each valid output.
